answers.question: Does every producer map to a consumer and every consumer to a producer or schedule?
answers.answer: No. 15 BullMQ queues/15 workers are 1:1 registered, but only 10 of 15 jobs have a production producer. mi-exif, mi-search-index, graph-domain-sync, graph-timeline-sync and org-health-refresh have consumers and no producer (6 worker enqueue helpers exported with zero callers). report-dlq has producers and no consumer (by design); media-intelligence-dlq has neither. All 19 registered sweeps are started.

answers.question: Do queue payloads carry caller-controlled tenant/authority?
answers.answer: No for canonical jobs. Producers can only set commandId/traceId (buildCanonicalJobPayload); consumers decode via decodeCanonicalJobPayload which rejects unknown keys and flags authority-shaped fields; every consumer re-derives the workspace from the named durable row. Legacy pre-Point-5 payloads are drained with authority fields discarded. report-dlq is a raw diagnostic payload with no consumer.

answers.question: Is the durable row committed before enqueue (no ack-before-durable-write)?
answers.answer: Yes for report (ReportGenerationRequest created then enqueued outside tx), redaction (row QUEUED before enqueue), derived asset (row upserted PENDING first), MI (run row inserted first). OTS/purge use the Evidence row itself. Enqueue never throws; failure leaves the row for a reconciler - except derived assets (no reconciler) and OTS PENDING (no reconciler).

answers.question: Can a report retry create a second Report row or a second custody event?
answers.answer: No. Version is reserved under pg_advisory_xact_lock on the request row; a retry of a REPORT_COMMITTED request routes to PACKAGE_FOR_VERSION; the custody events, Evidence update and Report.create are in ONE commit transaction that re-checks the reservation and the (evidenceId,version) uniqueness; losing commit throws REPORT_RESERVATION_LOST_RETRY leaving only an unreferenced immutable object.

answers.question: Stuck after worker crash - which sweep recovers each family?
answers.answer: Report: lease 15m released by lifecycle-recovery then re-enqueued (recovers ~20m). MI runs: 20m lease released by intelligence-run reconciler. Redaction: NOT recovered (RENDERING has no lease reclaim). OTS: stalled job is re-run by BullMQ, but a PENDING row whose follow-up was lost is never re-enqueued. Derived asset: no reconciler. Purge: trash-grace hourly. Exchange package: 30m ON CONFLICT lease. Redis cron lock TTL fixed 10m, no renewal, fail-open on Redis error.

answers.question: Races between report/package/TSA/OTS jobs; stale evidence version?
answers.answer: Report and package share one request and the per-evidence advisory lock; OTS writes are compare-and-set on the full OTS snapshot (a stale observation is discarded). The report renders the Evidence OTS columns as of issuance and is not regenerated when OTS later anchors (the 'ots_upgrade_completed' purpose has no producer). TSA is not queued. Report claim blocks on governance policy-version change (BLOCKED_STALE).

evidence.snippet: const res = await tx.evidence.updateMany({ where: otsSnapshotWhere(evidenceId, row),

answers.question: Infinite retry / infinite recovery loops?
answers.answer: BullMQ attempts are bounded everywhere (max 20 for OTS). But two reconciler loops are unbounded: MI runs of kinds that never write the run row are re-enqueued every 10 min forever (QUEUES-03), and every semantic chunk aged 30min-30d is re-enqueued every 10 min because the owed predicate reads a column nobody writes (QUEUES-10). Report requests are bounded by REPORT_RECONCILE_MAX_ATTEMPTS=12.

answers.question: Are workers prevented from claiming jobs until secrets/signer/object-lock are verified?
answers.answer: Only the report worker (autorun:false, started after validatePackageSignerAtStartup). The other 14 workers autorun on construction at module load and 4 sweeps are started at import, before initSecretsAuthority, signer validation and object-lock bootstrap.

answers.question: Does the registry's per-job timeoutMs bound a single attempt?
answers.answer: No. RetryPolicy.timeoutMs is declared but never passed to BullMQ nor enforced by any processor; long attempts are bounded only by per-call timeouts (e.g. ots execFile timeout) and by DB leases.

findings.title: OTS initialization schedules its follow-up upgrade onto its own active job, so every newly stamped proof stays PENDING with no future upgrade and no automatic recovery

evidence.snippet: if (isLiveQueueJobState(state)) { return { enqueued: true, jobId, collapsed: true };
await enqueueOtsUpgradeJob(evidenceId, { delayMs: 60 * 60 * 1000, traceId: "ots_followup", selfJobId: job.id,

findings.observed: Finalization enqueues job ots-upgrade-<E>. That job finds no proof, calls ensureEvidenceOtsInitialized (writes otsProofBase64 + otsStatus PENDING), then enqueues the follow-up WITHOUT selfJobId. enqueueCanonicalJob finds job ots-upgrade-<E> (itself) in state 'active', treats it as a live duplicate and returns {enqueued:true, collapsed:true} without adding anything. The job then completes. No upgrade is ever scheduled. The only automatic OTS reconciler selects rows where otsStatus IS NULL AND otsProofBase64 IS NULL, so the now-PENDING row is invisible to it.
findings.expected: After initialization a delayed upgrade poll must exist until the proof anchors or the global budget is exhausted; the self-reschedule path at line 703 already passes selfJobId for exactly this reason.
findings.dataFlow: evidence-complete.service.ts:1454 -> ots-anchoring-authority.service.ts:85 -> BullMQ ots-upgrade -> ots-upgrade.processor.ts:344 ensureEvidenceOtsInitialized -> :351 enqueue (collapses) -> job completes -> Evidence.otsStatus=PENDING forever
findings.rootCause: Missing selfJobId on the post-initialization follow-up; the reconciler population excludes initialized-but-never-upgraded rows although the comment at :353-355 says 'the reconciliation path re-enqueues it'.
findings.blastRadius: Every record finalized through the normal path (every plan); OTS anchoring never progresses past the calendar-pending proof unless an operator uses Operations remediation.
findings.impact: Records are never Bitcoin-anchored; the OTS global budget is never evaluated (it only runs inside a job), so no budget-exhausted incident fires either. Only the API's aged-pending condition makes it visible.
findings.reproduction: Finalize an evidence with a reachable OTS calendar; after the first ots-upgrade job completes, inspect BullMQ: no delayed ots-upgrade-<E> or ots-upgrade-<E>-next-* job exists and evidence.ots_status remains PENDING indefinitely.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Local Redis + worker with a stub `ots` binary returning a pending proof: enqueue UpgradeOts for a finalized fixture evidence, wait for completion, assert otsUpgradeQueue.getDelayed() is empty and ots_upgraded_at_utc never changes.
findings.remediation: Pass selfJobId: job.id at ots-upgrade.processor.ts:351 (and check/log the returned outcome); extend the OTS reconciler to also select otsStatus='PENDING' rows whose ots_upgraded_at_utc (or proof creation) is older than the poll interval and that have no live job.
findings.acceptanceProof: Integration test against real Redis: after an initialization job completes, exactly one delayed job exists for the evidence; reconciler re-enqueues a PENDING row with no live job.
findings.migrationBackfill: Run the (extended) reconciler or repair-ots-hybrid-state script over all otsStatus=PENDING rows to re-enter the ladder.

findings.title: OTS self-reschedule alternates between a fixed id and a fixed '-next-' id; on the third hop the add targets a retained completed job id, BullMQ silently ignores it, and the ladder stops while reporting success

evidence.snippet: BullMQ IGNORES an `add` whose jobId already exists — INCLUDING a retained completed or failed job — and still returns a Job object.
await enqueueOtsUpgradeJob(evidenceId, { ... selfJobId: job.id, });   // result not inspected

findings.observed: The discriminated id is a pure function of the evidence id, so it is the same string every time. Hop 1: X (ots-upgrade-E) schedules Xn. Hop 2: Xn runs, getJob(X) is completed, it is removed and X re-added. Hop 3: X runs, isSelfReference -> jobId = Xn; the self-reference branch does not check or remove an existing Xn, and Xn is still retained as completed (last 100 completions kept). queue.add is ignored, the function returns enqueued:true, and the return value is not inspected at :703.
findings.expected: Every self-reschedule must result in a runnable job or an honest failure the caller acts on.
findings.dataFlow: ots-upgrade.processor.ts:703 -> queue.ts:501 enqueueCanonicalJob(selfJobId) -> enqueue.ts:152-158 -> queue.add(existing completed id) -> no-op
findings.rootCause: The selfJobId exception skips the collapse-or-replace handling applied to every other id, and the discriminator is deterministic rather than unique per hop.
findings.blastRadius: Any evidence that reaches three upgrade hops (including records re-entered by operator remediation after QUEUES-01) while the OTS queue has <100 completions between hops.
findings.impact: Anchoring silently halts after ~2-3 hours of polling; Bitcoin confirmation typically needs longer, so proofs remain PENDING.
findings.reproduction: With low queue volume, trigger remediation for a PENDING evidence and observe jobs ots-upgrade-E, ots-upgrade-E-next-..., ots-upgrade-E, then nothing.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Unit test enqueueCanonicalJob against a real Redis/BullMQ queue: run three simulated hops with removeOnComplete=100 and assert the third add creates a waiting/delayed job (it will not).
findings.remediation: In the self-reference branch, apply the same getJob/getState/remove handling to the discriminated id, or use a per-hop unique id (hop counter from the job data or attemptsMade), and act on enqueued:false.
findings.acceptanceProof: Real-Redis test of 5 consecutive self-reschedules each producing a delayed job.

findings.title: A redaction derivative that hits a transient storage error or a worker crash after its claim is stuck in RENDERING forever; retries, the reconciler and a user re-request all skip it

evidence.snippet: where: { id: derivativeId, state: "QUEUED" }, data: { state: "RENDERING", renderStartedAt: new Date() },
// Reset for a fresh render attempt. RENDERING/QUEUED rows are left untouched

findings.observed: The claim moves QUEUED->RENDERING. A transient error rethrows for BullMQ retry, but the retry's claim requires QUEUED, returns not_queued, and the job completes as a no-op. A crash mid-render has the same outcome via stall re-delivery. Nothing ever moves RENDERING back: the reconciler scans QUEUED, the API re-request only resets FAILED/PENDING, and versionId is UNIQUE so no new derivative can be created. The registry declares a 20-minute renderStartedAtUtc lease that no code implements.
findings.expected: RENDERING older than the lease must be reclaimable (by the retry and by the reconciler) or failed with a reason.
findings.dataFlow: API create QUEUED -> job claim RENDERING -> S3 5xx throw -> retry claim_skipped -> job completed -> row RENDERING forever
findings.rootCause: Claim predicate has no expired-lease arm; reconciler population excludes RENDERING.
findings.blastRadius: Any redaction render hitting a transient S3/network error or worker restart.
findings.impact: The redacted deliverable can never be produced for that version; the UI shows rendering indefinitely.
findings.reproduction: Make putObject fail with ETIMEDOUT once; derivative remains RENDERING after all retries.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Local PG+Redis with a storage double failing the first PUT with ETIMEDOUT: run the job with attempts=3 and assert final state RENDERING and job completed.
findings.remediation: Allow claim from RENDERING when renderStartedAt < now-20m; add RENDERING-lease arm to the reconciler (reset to QUEUED or FAILED); on retryable throw, reset to QUEUED before rethrowing.
findings.acceptanceProof: Test: transient failure then retry produces READY; crashed claim older than lease is recovered by the reconciler.
findings.migrationBackfill: Reset RENDERING rows with renderStartedAt older than 20 min to QUEUED.

findings.title: Trash-grace reconciler re-reads the same oldest 200 TRASHED rows every hour; once 200 of them are blocked (hold, retention, object lock, approval pending) eligible records are never purged, and the purge job's own BLOCKED reschedule is a no-op

evidence.snippet: const rows = await prisma.evidence.findMany({ where: { lifecycleState: "TRASHED", deleteScheduledForUtc: { lte: now },
enqueued += 1;   // counted regardless of enqueue outcome
await enqueueEvidencePurgeJob(evidence.id, recheckAt.toISOString());   // from inside the running evidence-purge-<id> job

findings.observed: The candidate query has no cursor and does not exclude rows that stay blocked; blocked rows keep lifecycleState TRASHED and past-due deleteScheduledForUtc, so they sort first on every tick. DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=200. The purge processor's BLOCKED path enqueues the same deterministic id while that job is active, which collapses (enqueue.ts:161) and schedules nothing, so trash-grace is the only producer.

findings.title: 14 of 15 BullMQ workers and 4 sweeps start claiming work at module import, before secrets hydration, package-signer validation and object-lock bootstrap

All other workers begin fetching jobs as soon as the module evaluates, and redaction/trash-grace/search-index/intelligence-run schedulers are started at top level.
